identity.real_world_identity_notes: An archived General Motors specification identifies a six-speed sequential-manual transaxle for the 2003 C5-R. AMS2 cockpit inspection confirms a six-speed sequential stick without paddles, while the exact represented chassis year remains unspecified.

wheel_rim.notes: Direct cockpit inspection showed a round rim without an integrated display; exact diameter remains unknown.

notes: With Auto Clutch disabled, the car stalled when moving from rest without physical clutch input.
All six sequential-stick gears accepted clutch-free full-throttle upshifts with automatic throttle cut.
Clutch-free downshifts were accepted and no automatic throttle blip was observed; authentic rev matching therefore requires the driver to blip the throttle manually.
The exact Low Downforce identity inherits the verified base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.
Base car live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with Auto Clutch disabled.
Standing-start clutch, six-speed sequential stick without paddles, automatic cut, no automatic blip, and round no-display rim were directly observed.
Low Downforce inherits the base controls as an approved aero-package assumption and was not separately live-tested.

confidence.basis: Exact simulator identity, cockpit controls, and technique were directly tested; archived manufacturer specifications independently support the six-speed sequential hardware family.

The official PMR article is explicitly titled for the 2004 Chevrolet Corvette C5.R and states that the 2004 car adopted an Xtrac six-speed sequential gearbox. A contemporary General Motors 2004 program release independently identifies the factory C5-R's new six-speed Xtrac gearbox, and the repository already contains the matching curated Chevrolet Corvette C5-R record. The exact PMR H-pattern result is therefore treated as an implementation discrepancy, not as evidence for a separate early C5-R identity.
